note: Public standards only. SAE J1939 SPN/FMI and OBD-II/EOBD P-codes are published and shared across all makes. Manufacturer-specific tables (Cat E-codes and CID/FMI, Komatsu CA/E-codes, Hitachi, JCB, Volvo MID/PID/SID) are proprietary and deliberately not reproduced here.

fmi.0: Data valid but above normal operating range — most severe level
fmi.1: Data valid but below normal operating range — most severe level
fmi.3: Voltage above normal, or shorted to a high source
fmi.4: Voltage below normal, or shorted to a low source
fmi.5: Current below normal, or open circuit
fmi.6: Current above normal, or grounded circuit
fmi.7: Mechanical system not responding, or out of adjustment
fmi.8: Abnormal frequency, pulse width or period
fmi.15: Data valid but above normal operating range — least severe level
fmi.16: Data valid but above normal operating range — moderately severe level
fmi.17: Data valid but below normal operating range — least severe level
fmi.18: Data valid but below normal operating range — moderately severe level

families.label: SAE J1939 (SPN / FMI)
families.hint: Standard across diesel engines and most modern plant. SPN says which parameter, FMI says what is wrong with it.

families.label: OBD-II / EOBD (P-codes)
families.hint: P0 and P2 codes are standardised. P1 and P3 ranges are left to each manufacturer.

families.label: Caterpillar (E-code or CID-FMI)
families.hint: Cat event codes such as E1601 and CID/FMI pairs come from Cat's own tables, which are licensed, not public.

families.label: Komatsu (CA or E-code)
families.hint: Komatsu codes such as CA559 or E02 map through Komatsu's own service tables.

families.label: Volvo / older J1587 (MID-PID-SID)
families.hint: MID identifies the module, then PID or SID with an FMI. Partly standardised, partly maker-specific.

families.label: Maker-specific
families.hint: Hitachi, JCB, Kubota, Deere and most attachment controllers each use their own numbering.
